newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures struggled to make ground despite a buoyant U.S. bond market as few wanted to take long positions after the relentless rally this month.

Traders said without the U.S. bond market support, the market could well have slipped further, although most remained bullish about the prospects for French bonds even if there were a short-term correction.
"It's bull congestion," said the head of bond trading at a U.S. house in Paris.
"Too many people are long, the market needs to purge itself," said a futures trader in Paris.
French Prime Minister Alain Juppe and German Chancellor Helmut Kohl earlier issued a joint statement saying the franc was fairly valued against the mark.

Analysts said while clearly designed to calm market speculation about a weakening of the French franc fort policy, it was probably also an attempt to shift the debate from the franc and towards the strength of the mark against the dollar.
"It's probably to try and calm down the markets as the franc's been under pressure," Joanne Perez, strategist at Merrill Lynch in Paris said.

"It's also an attempt to try and shift the debate away from Mark/Paris to dollar/Mark and the future strength of the euro," she said. "This has all come about because the dollar is weaker than they want it to be and it's not clear the United States is going to bail them out."

The franc later fell as low as 3.3924. A foreign exchange trader said earlier he though losses would be limited below 3.3920 as there were French corporates looking to off load marks around that level.
Some traders also said a few players had been punting on a collapse in the franc by buying cheap mark call options with expiry dates of up to a year with a strike price of 3.70 francs.
The Bank of France left interest rates unchanged as expected at its regular money market tender on Thursday.
